W.note: Lines count 5-7-5 exactly (Sil-ver threads at dusk / clouds no com-mon sky can make / hang where no one looks), and silver-at-dusk evokes noctilucent clouds, but 'no one looks' is a vague, generic turn and the imagery stays thin.

X.note: Counts are 5-7-5 exactly (Lens cloud on the ridge / the wind pours through it all day / the cloud does not move), and it names a lenticular cloud accurately: a stationary cloud over a ridge while wind streams through it, a fresh paradox that lands on its flat final line.

Y.note: Line 1 is 5 syllables, but line 2 ('the cloud's edge turns mother-of-pearl') runs 8 and line 3 ('then the blue takes it back') runs 6, so the 5-7-5 shape is broken; the nacreous image after sunset is accurate and the closing turn is strong, though mother-of-pearl is a familiar simile.

Z.note: Exact 5-7-5 (Na-cre-ous light blooms / high above the fro-zen fjord / a cloud gone by dawn), accurately evoking nacreous polar stratospheric clouds lit after sunset and gone by morning, with a clean ephemeral close; 'blooms' and 'frozen fjord' lean toward stock phrasing.
